title: A sprint close, a CI read and an intake run leave an ops row
goal: backlog.py close appends one ops sprint.close row (counts of items landed and dropped, bugs filed, provisional answers confirmed, refused dones, planned-to-closed time) before it deletes the items; red-pipeline and the delivery CI check append a ci.pipeline row only when a pipeline's state changes, with the job-list call count; intake appends an intake.detect row when a detector found something or hit its budget, with its coverage.

gates.question: This adds a mechanism before a failure it answers has happened (backlog.md, Changing this process). Add it anyway?

notes: Failures it answers: close deletes the items, so per-sprint facts survive only in the commit body (a retrospective had to read git); red-pipeline made up to 100 job-list calls unseen (BG-h4wygoak); drift skipped items for want of coverage data (BG-3q6fviow).
